- First enter a child session with \<leader\> +down
- Then use bare right/left arrows (without leader) to cycle between children

## Root Cause Analysis

The crash originates in `packages/app/src/components/session/session-header.tsx` at line 306:

```typescript
const current = createMemo(() => options().find((o) => o.id === prefs.app) ?? options()[0])
```

`current()` returns `undefined` when `options()` is temporarily empty — which happens during startup before the file-manager/app list resolves, or during project switching. Downstream accesses like `current().id`, `current().label`, and `current().icon` (lines 421, 423, 428, 458) then throw the `TypeError`.

## Fix

Add a hardcoded fallback so `current()` is never `undefined`:

```typescript
const current = createMemo(
  () => options().find((o) => o.id === prefs.app) ?? options()[0] ?? { id: "finder", label: "Finder", icon: "finder" } as const
)
```

This is the same defensive pattern used in PR #16476 (`props.text?.length ?? 0`) and PR #16475 (`createMemo(() => props.text ?? "")`) which fix the structurally identical `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')` crash in `TextShimmer` (issue #16473).

## Related

- #16467 — same `current()` undefined crash, triggered by fast project switching
- #16323 — broader `<Show>` stale-read analysis; `session-header.tsx` is listed as one of the unfixed files
- #16473 / PR #16475 / PR #16476 — identical pattern in `TextShimmer`

A PR fixing this is incoming.

## Confirmed Root Cause

This is the same bug as #16459. The crash is in `packages/app/src/components/session/session-header.tsx` line 306:

```typescript
const current = createMemo(() => options().find((o) => o.id === prefs.app) ?? options()[0])
```

During project switching, `options()` briefly becomes an empty array (race condition between cleanup and re-render), so `options()[0]` returns `undefined`. The subsequent `current().id` access on line 421 throws.

## Proposed Fix

```typescript
const current = createMemo(
  () => options().find((o) => o.id === prefs.app) ?? options()[0] ?? { id: "finder", label: "Finder", icon: "finder" } as const
)
```

The hardcoded fallback `{ id: "finder", ... }` ensures `current()` is always a valid object. This is safer than the PR description's suggestion because it doesn't require changing the downstream call sites — `current().id` remains safe without optional chaining.

A fix PR is incoming that addresses this.

## Root Cause

The crash is in `packages/ui/src/components/text-shimmer.tsx` lines 40 and 47:

```typescript
const shimmerSize = createMemo(() => {
  const len = Math.max(props.text.length, 1)  // crashes if props.text is undefined
  ...
})
const shimmerDuration = createMemo(() => {
  const len = Math.max(props.text.length, 1)  // same
  ...
})
```

`props.text` is typed as `string` but can be `undefined` at runtime when the reactive value feeding it (e.g. i18n translation) hasn't resolved yet during initial evaluation.

## Two PRs addressing this

- **PR #16476** — minimal fix: `props.text?.length ?? 0` (optional chaining)
- **PR #16475** — structural fix: wraps in `createMemo(() => props.text ?? "")` and extracts shared `len` memo

Both are valid. PR #16475's approach is slightly more idiomatic for SolidJS (memoized fallback) and eliminates the duplicated `len` computation.

## Status Update

The `startTransition` removal in `cf425d11` (PR #16236) mitigated the most common trigger, but the 17+ unfixed `<Show>` instances listed in this issue remain.

More immediately, the `session-header.tsx` component has a separate but related crash (#16459, #16467): `current()` returns `undefined` when `options()` is empty, causing `current().id` to throw. A fix PR is incoming for that specific crash.

The broader `keyed` fix was reverted (`2094e8b2`, `eeeb21ff`) on Mar 5 — likely due to side effects from changing `item()` → `item` in callback bodies. Any future `keyed` fix attempt needs to ensure all `item()` accessor calls inside the callback are updated to `item` (direct value) simultaneously.

## Additional Detail

After patching the `project.worktree` column in the database and restarting, the correct worktree branch **does appear briefly** on startup, but then **reverts back to the main repo branch mid-session** (during agent thinking/processing).

This suggests there is a background git polling or project refresh cycle that re-derives the branch by following `--git-common-dir` rather than staying scoped to the worktree's working directory. The initial resolution is correct, but it gets overwritten by a subsequent refresh.

Closing in favor of a new feature request that reframes this as a capability gap rather than a bug. The core ask remains the same: make the Bash tool's prompt guidance adapt to the detected Windows shell.

These two issues share the same direction (cross-project context sharing) but differ significantly in scope and complexity:

- **#10300** proposes a heavyweight, real-time bidirectional session bridge — two linked sessions continuously query each other's full context, like a monorepo experience for multi-repo setups.
- **This issue (#16483)** proposes a lightweight, fire-and-forget local pub/sub — `/beam` broadcasts a selected slice of conversation to the local filesystem, `/catch` imports it into another session. No persistent link, no real-time sync, fully decoupled.

This could serve as a **pragmatic MVP** toward the broader vision in #10300 — simple enough to implement quickly (local files, no IPC), useful enough to validate whether cross-project context transfer is worth investing in further.

@tobeycodes Yes, that's correct — with one important nuance.

When you run `opencode web`, the server starts locally but the UI assets (HTML/JS/CSS) are **proxied live from `https://app.opencode.ai`** via the catch-all route in [`server.ts:564-579`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/server/server.ts#L564-L579). So the frontend version you get is whatever is currently deployed to `app.opencode.ai`, not the version that matches your local `opencode` binary.

This means:
- **You can't pin the UI version** by staying on an older `opencode` binary — the frontend always comes from the live CDN
- **Fixes deployed to `app.opencode.ai`** will reach you immediately without a binary update
- The crash in this issue will be resolved once PR [#16478](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/16478) (or a similar fix) is merged and deployed to `app.opencode.ai`

The **Desktop app** (Tauri) is different — it bundles the UI assets locally, so the version is pinned to the release you installed.
